data.one_liner: Simultaneously downloads, caches, and streams remote content via a local HTTP server.
data.what_it_does: Simultaneously downloads, caches, and streams remote web content. It sets up a local HTTP server so standard media players and plugins can immediately play media while it is still downloading.
use_when: You want media players to play remote audio or video files instantly while downloading.
You need persistent offline caching for streaming resources.
You want range request support for seeking in media players.
avoid_when: Your target environment does not permit cleartext local traffic or local server binding.
You only need basic asset or file downloading without streaming or media playback integration.
strengths: Allows instant playback of remote media while downloading.
Works seamlessly with existing media player plugins via local HTTP URLs.
Supports range requests, resumable downloads, and custom headers.
weaknesses: Requires platform-specific configuration for cleartext traffic and local HTTP server usage.
Local server sockets can be reclaimed on iOS when the app enters the background, requiring manual reactivation handling.
data.setup_notes: Requires platform configuration to allow cleartext (non-HTTPS) traffic to localhost. iOS/macOS requires an NSAppTransportSecurity entry in Info.plist, and Android requires a network security configuration XML file.

alternatives.name: just_audio
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you specifically need advanced built-in audio playback and caching capabilities without setting up an external proxy server.

alternatives.name: video_player
alternatives.why_pick_it: If you prefer using platform-native caching options built directly into video player implementations.
